entries.title: Proverbs 1:2
segments:
vv 2-4. 
 
  To know--to perceive--to receive; written that those who read them may know, perceive, and receive. 
 
  To give; written that they may give. 
 
  Wisdom--instruction, etc.; these are all different terms for describing true wisdom and righteousness, which consist in knowing and doing the will of God, and can never be separated. 
 
  To receive--justice, and judgment, and equity; to learn in what they consist, and to conform our life to them. 
 
  Subtilty--discretion; a quick discernment between what is wise and foolish.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:5
segments:
A wise man--a man of understanding; one who understands the worth of knowledge. 
 
  Shall attain; by hearing and learning. 
 
They who have wisdom understand the worth of knowledge, and earnestly seek it; but fools despise all instruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:6
segments: Dark sayings; sayings expressed in an enigmatical or obscure way, and requiring study to understand their meaning.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:7
segments:
The beginning of knowledge; lying at its foundation. 
 
  Fools; who have no fear of God. 
 
They who would be truly wise must begin by devoting themselves to God's service, and making his word the rule of their life.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:9
segments: Chains about thy neck; worn as badges of honor.  Chains of gold were common as decorations of princes.
Reverence for parental instruction in the child makes the man prosperous and honored.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:10
segments: They who choose the wicked for their companions become like them in character and end.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:17
segments:
vv 17-18. 
 
  Surely in vain the net is spread; the fowler does not expect a bird to be caught in a snare which he sees; but these sinners, and all who go with them, are spreading a net for their own souls.  The young should imitate the prudence of the birds in avoiding it.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:19
segments:
So are the ways; such is the issue to which they lead. 
 
  Greedy of gain; unlawfully desires gain, and seeks it by unlawful means. 
 
  Taketh away the life; by leading them into a snare.
Unrighteous gain has destroyed millions; but has never made one man permanently prosperous and happy.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:20
segments:
Wisdom; the wisdom of God addressing men.  It includes all the revelations of himself which God has made to men.  And since these are all made through Christ, who spoke before his advent by the prophets, and afterwards by the apostles, we may say that wisdom speaks here as the eternal Word, who is the only revealer of God to men. Joh 1.18 
 
God urges upon men his lessons of heavenly wisdom in so many ways, that none can remain ignorant of them but those who obstinately refuse to hear.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:21
segments: Chief place of concourse--the gates--the city; she cries in the most public and frequented places.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:23
segments: I will pour out my spirit unto you; she speaks in God's name, and her spirit is God's Spirit.  Compare

entries.title: Proverbs 1:24
segments: Stretched out my hand; the gesture of earnest entreaty.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:28
segments: There is a point in rebellion against God and neglect of his warnings, beyond which the sinner's destruction is certain and irremediable.

entries.title: Proverbs 1:31
segments:
The fruit of their own way; terror and destruction, the proper recompense of setting at naught the counsels of wisdom. 
 
The sinner is responsible for his own ruin.  The destruction which comes upon him is the proper result of his perverseness in refusing to hear and obey God.
